pieces.text: Ask whether a prepaid funeral plan exists. Many people have one and never mention it.

alt: A timeline card of the first 48 hours after a parent dies, from getting the death pronounced to checking Social Security was told, beside a note about prepaid funeral plans.
caption: The first 48 hours, in order. The rest of the two weeks follows in the guide.

steps.what: Buy more copies than feels needed
Use Tell Us Once, if it applies

alt: A timeline card for the first week after a parent dies in the UK, beside a card comparing what Tell Us Once covers against what you still have to contact yourself.
caption: The first week in the UK: register first, then Tell Us Once covers most of government in one go.

items: Annual payments are easy to miss

alt: A table of three free US tools for finding life insurance, dormant accounts and lost pensions, beside a checklist for reading a year of bank statements.
caption: Three of the four free tools worth trying, example matches, before you pay for a search.

steps.what: Search it before letters are issued

pieces.text: The most recent valid one usually governs. Keep the older one anyway.

alt: A timeline card showing where to search for a will, at home, with the attorney, in a deposit box, then the probate court, beside a note about keeping an older will.
caption: The search order that turns up most wills, the probate court last.

pieces.text: Decline before you act. Once letters are issued, stepping back needs a court petition.

alt: A checklist card of an executor's first week, from certified death certificates to opening a separate estate bank account, beside a note that you can decline before you start acting.
caption: The first week, roughly in order. Decline before this point if you cannot take it on.

items: The original will, not a copy
Details of any funeral plan paid

pieces.text: Look for creditors before you distribute anything. Executors can be personally liable.

alt: A checklist of what an executor should ask for immediately, from certified certificates to the original will and bank statements, with a note about creditors.
caption: You can decline, as long as you have not already started acting as executor.

pieces.text: Passwords and account numbers. Write where the recovery kit is kept instead.

alt: A checklist of five areas in an if-something-happens-to-me file, from who to contact first to what you'd want, with a note that passwords stay out and locations go in.
caption: Five of the eight areas. Each line says where something is, never what's inside it.

pieces.text: These accounts pay whoever is named on the form, not whoever the will names.

alt: A comparison card showing a life insurance policy paying a current spouse and an old 401(k) still paying an ex-spouse, though the will names the same person for both.
caption: An example. The will says the same thing for both accounts; the forms decide differently.

pieces.title: If something happens
rows: How to get into my phone

alt: A blank lined page titled If something happens, with five prompts: who to call first, where the will is, phone access, what's due this week, who relies on me.
caption: Five lines, all places and names. No passwords.

pieces.text: Set it up while you're alive. A death certificate alone rarely opens an account.

alt: A table comparing Apple and Google accounts with and without a legacy contact set up, showing photos and chosen data become reachable only with advance setup.
caption: General patterns for major US providers. Confirm with each provider directly.

pieces.text: Shred anything with an account number, a signature or a full address.

alt: A table card showing how long to keep tax records, certificates, pay stubs and a home deed, beside a note to shred anything with an account number.
caption: Three folders, a shred pile, and the documents worth keeping forever.

lines.label: Yourself
lines.text: I've been sorting my paperwork. Have you done yours?

lines.label: A what-if
lines.text: If we were both in the hospital, could we write the basics down?

alt: A script card with two conversation openers about a parent's paperwork, beside a checklist of what to ask about: the will, the bank, power of attorney, medical decisions.
caption: Two ways to start, and four things to ask about by location, not detail.

pieces.text: Passwords and account numbers. Write where the recovery kit is instead.

alt: A checklist of the first five tabs of a life admin binder, with a note that passwords and account numbers stay out and locations go in.
caption: Five of the eight tabs. Each page holds locations and names.

pieces.text: $131 is paid by hand. Write down which bills those are and how someone could log in.

alt: A ledger of five example bills in a two-week hospital stay, three paying automatically and two by hand, totaling $1,951, with a note about the manual ones.
caption: An example month. Amounts are invented to show the split.

steps.what: Ask them before you name them
Write down where the form is kept

alt: A timeline card showing the order for naming a health care agent, choose, ask, talk, record, beside a card comparing an emergency contact to a health care agent.
caption: The order that works, and how a health care agent differs from an emergency contact.

items: Think values and daily life first
Ask them before you name them

lines.label: You say
lines.text: If something happened to both of us, would you raise the kids?

lines.label: Backup
lines.text: We're also asking you to be the backup, just so you know.

alt: A checklist card for naming a guardian, from thinking about values to naming them in a will, beside a script card for asking someone to take on the role.
caption: The checklist, and two ways to actually ask them.

alt: A table listing who to notify after a death, from close family through Social Security, banks and credit bureaus, with what each needs and when, beside a short checklist of what can wait.
caption: Who to notify and what can wait, in order. Example order only.

pieces.text: Health coverage changes have a 60-day window from the event, not from when you get to it.

alt: A table of life events, marriage, divorce, a new baby and a new job, next to what to look at again for each, beside a note about the 60-day health coverage deadline.
caption: Where to look again, by event.

items: What it is, in plain words
Who can open it: a name

pieces.text: Never the combination, the PIN, or where the key is. Only who'd find out how.

alt: A checklist card of what to record about a safe or deposit box, beside a note warning never to write down the combination or PIN.
caption: What to write about a safe, box or spare key, and what never to write.

items: What they need day to day

pieces.text: A will can name a caregiver. A pet trust adds a trustee and funding for the animal.

alt: A checklist card of what to write down for each pet, from who would take them to where the vet records are, beside a note about pet trusts.
caption: What to write for each animal, and when a trust does more than a note.
